name: goat-shelter

purpose.why: Rebuilt on Evan's request (2026-10-22) to replace the Ranch tile's original model with a crafted one, keeping its game role.
purpose.audience: children building and playing in a miniature ranch
purpose.style: normal (upgrade: the same asset, built better)

brief.prompt: a small timber goat shelter, rose-pink plank walls, a teal shingled gable roof, a low open doorway with a wooden ramp, a raised plank platform beside it for goats to climb on, a small hay rack

concept.tool: Midjourney web app (midjourney.com/imagine), driven in Evan's signed-in Chrome by Claude through the Claude in Chrome extension, one job at a time, text prompts only (no image reference)

hero.prompt: a small timber goat shelter, rose-pink plank walls, a teal shingled gable roof, a low open doorway with a wooden ramp, a raised plank platform beside it for goats to climb on, a small hay rack, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 1:1
hero.pick_reason: low doorway with wooden ramp and raised plank platform, crisp shape

turnaround.prompt: orthographic turnaround sheet, front view, side view, back view, evenly spaced, same scale, a small timber goat shelter, rose-pink plank walls, a teal shingled gable roof, a low open doorway with a wooden ramp, a raised plank platform beside it for goats to climb on, a small hay rack, stylized 3D game asset, low-poly diorama style, flat painted colors, soft studio lighting, plain warm cream background, centered, full object visible, no text --ar 16:9
turnaround.pick_reason: front, three-quarter side and back of one shelter with ramp and platform, cleanly separated. upscale_clicked is approximate and the download was delayed about 95 minutes by a lost browser-extension connection, not by Midjourney

construction.by: modeler agent, directed by the art director (Claude)

rounds.change: First build: 2.4 x 2.75 m, eave 1.72, 45 deg, 0.34 m eaves, stilts 0.30, ramp 1.45, platform 1.1 m deep. Views made (front stretched, back re-cropped and mirrored, side dropped). Hero scored on the raw mj hero, whose mask included the ground shadow (0.583 at a 40/12 guess, 0.708 at the best grid camera).

Compact plan (D 1.95), stilts 0.34, ramp 1.6, platform 1.25 deep at 0.48, taller bargeboards over the deck edge, apex blocks. Hero target re-keyed by hue (shadow out, ramp in); camera recalibrated to 45 deg / 12 deg.
Shingles no longer poke through the bargeboards; the bargeboards half-lap at the crossing (fixes a black z-fighting diamond at the apex).
D 2.2, side eaves 0.26, attic backing boards (plank gaps were see-through in the gables), pink boarded roof deck/soffit.
D 2.4, ramp 1.8, narrower platform, lower side rail.
D back to 2.2 (the hero prefers it).
Chunkier, fewer shingle tabs (0.40 m courses, 0.38 to 0.56 m tabs, thicker butts), ramp 1.65, warmer, duller hay.
Tried taller stilts (0.42) and eave 1.80 with 0.32 m side eaves: the sheet views improved, the hero got worse.
Stilts and eave back to 0.34 / 1.72, kept the 0.32 m side eaves; platform back to 1.32 m wide, ramp 1.6; sills inset and stilt tops lifted 2 cm to remove coplanar black slivers.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and score; to_game.py goat-shelter.

what_was_done: The gable end with the tall open doorway faces -Y. The door sits right of centre (x 0.16 to 0.92), the climbing platform fills the space left of it, the ramp runs from the doorway straight out to -Y, and the window is on the +X long side. That is the side the hero shows, which is also the side the harness hero camera sees.

views/view_front.png is mj view_front with the cast-shadow ground strip and the loose rack left of the shed cut away, then stretched horizontally (x1.35) so that apex height over wall width matches the hero (1.38). This pulls the sheet's ~64 deg roof towards the hero's pitch. views/view_back.png is re-cropped from turnaround.png, because split.py cut the right-hand building in two. That building is a 3/4 view of the back gable, so its right (pure gable) half is mirrored over the left half, the stray bench and ground strip are cut, and it is stretched the same way (x1.52). The side view is dropped: the sheet's middle view is a 3/4 front view, not an orthographic side. views/hero.png is the mj hero keyed by hue. The harness mask kept the hero's dark contact shadow under the stilts and dropped the grey-teal ramp, so the hero would have scored against the wrong shape.

hero_check.py renders from the hero's own direction: 45 deg off the front towards +X and 12 deg up, with the harness lens and distance. The direction was calibrated over a 7x6 yaw/elevation grid (hero_check.py calibrate) on the round-2 model and held fixed after that. The harness hero camera at (0.62, -0.78, 0.42) looks down much more steeply than the hero does.

Walls 2.4 x 2.2 m. Chunky 0.24 m rose corner posts run on down as stilts, so the sill sits 0.34 m off the ground (floor top 0.52 m). Plates and tie beams are at 1.72 m. The roof is 45 deg with 0.32 m side eaves and 0.30 m / 0.24 m gable overhangs. The rose bargeboards are 0.17 x 0.40 m, cover the deck edge and run 0.36 m past the apex, where they half-lap into an X. A rose ridge board sits between the two crossings. Total height is 3.43 m.

Two-tone rose vertical planks with alternating depth. A real doorway recess into a dark plank interior (a liner box with jamb and head reveals, and brown battens on the back wall that catch the light). A square window hole in the +X wall with a sill rail and head rail. Seven courses of chunky, jittered, lifted teal shingle tabs, with a pink boarded deck that shows under the overhangs as it does in the hero. Backing boards behind the gable triangles so that plank gaps never show through the attic. A 4-plank teal ramp 1.6 m long, with cleats on top and a brown trestle under it. A brown-timber platform 1.32 x 1.25 m with its deck at 0.48 m: legs, bearers, knee braces, 5 teal deck planks of uneven length, and a side rail. On the platform, a slatted hay crate with a heaped hay mound, loose straws and spilled hay. Grey stone pads under the stilts.

3,412 triangles (budget 9k, target 4 to 6k), 19 meshes, one flat material per mesh: Plank_Rose, Plank_RoseDark, Timber_Rose, Timber_Brown, Plank_Teal, Roof_Teal, Hay_Straw, Plank_Dark, Stone_Grey, Rope_String (planned only). No animation. The planned, foundation, frame, roof and complete variants come from the same build.py STATE groups. to_game.py goat-shelter ran cleanly.
construction.creative_additions: Grey stone pads under the stilts, cleats and a trestle on the ramp, knee braces under the platform, a few wisps of spilled hay beside the crate, brown battens inside the doorway so the dark recess reads as planked, and the platform's outline staked out in the planned stage.

geometry.up: Z (Blender source); Y in GLB and game
geometry.origin: centre of the footprint, on the ground

good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.839 from the hero's direction. The teal roof mass with crossed rose bargeboards, the stilts, the long ramp and the railed platform all read at tile size.
The back gable scores 0.841 against the mirrored sheet back. The walls, stilts and roof outline agree.

The construction stages read as a sequence: stakes and string lines (including the platform outline), then stone pads, stilts, sills and plank floor, then the rose post-and-beam frame with rafters and ridge beam, then the roof on the open frame, then the finished shed.
Well under budget at 3.4k triangles. Most of them go to the roof silhouette and the shingle tabs.
off: The front view scores 0.823, not more, because the sheet draws a steeper, concave roof whose eave tips droop to wall-top height. Per the AD, I kept the hero's straighter 45 deg pitch, which leaves blue along both rakes.

The proportions are a compromise between the hero numbers. A deeper plan (2.4 m) helped the sheet views but cost hero IoU, and so did taller stilts (0.42 m). I kept the 2.2 m depth and 0.34 m stilts that the hero prefers.
The hero's hay crate is a tapered basket with angled slats. Mine is a straight slatted box with a hay mound.
The hero's shingles are hand-carved slabs with bevelled edges. Mine are jittered flat-shaded blocks.
The hero camera direction was calibrated against this model, so the hero number is a guide, not ground truth.
The sheet's views are not true orthographic views of one building (two of them are 3/4 views), so both targets are rebuilt or stretched, and their IoU measures shape against the hero's proportions.

rights: Original work for Abbie's World. Concept art generated on Evan's Midjourney account; geometry generated procedurally, no third-party meshes or textures.
